theWindownAnalysis.whyTheRowIsRedInItsOwnWindow: Every row reads the SIBLING'S MAIN. The check-script-copies row's subject is THIS FILE, so while either main lacks the edited file, each PR's job compares its edited local copy to the sibling's unedited main and reports exactly one diff: check-script-copies. This is inherent to a self-referential byte-identity row; no merge order makes both PRs green before either merges.
theWindownAnalysis.whyItDoesNotBlock: MEASURED at source against the branch-protection API on 2026-09-19: `cross-repo literal drift` is NOT a required status check on either main. hauska-map requires only `No double-encoded source` and `test`; legacy-design-tools requires `Typecheck`, `Test`, `PR base is main`, `SS-W16 tier2 flood not served`, `SS-W18 api-server boots`. So the red window does not gate a landing.
theWindownAnalysis.whatSettlesIt: Once both mains carry the identical file, the post-merge push run in each repo and the nightly schedule (07:17Z map / 07:23Z LDT) read the settled pair. The first scheduled run after both merge is the predicate this lane cannot observe and hands back.
